chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Yahya ibn Abi al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one fasting during the journey in the month of Ramadan is like the one breaking the fast in it during residence.

Then he said: Indeed, a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, should I fast the month of Ramadan while traveling?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, it is easy upon me.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave charity to the sick of His community and its travelers with breaking the fast in the month of Ramadan. Would it not please one of you if He gave him a charity that he would like to return it?'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting while traveling during Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the principle of *al-rahma* (divine mercy) in legal concessions, where the traveler's voluntary fasting is not invalid but is treated as if they broke it, highlighting that accepting ease is a form of gratitude. The Prophet’s analogy of Allah’s concession being a 'charity' (*sadaqa*) implies that rejecting it out of stubbornness is akin to rejecting a gift, a nuance emphasized by scholars like Al-Kulayni to distinguish between mere permission and the preferred act. This reinforces the Shia view that the spirit of the law prioritizes well-being and divine pleasure over rigid asceticism when a specific concession is granted.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdul Malik Bin Utba, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Yahya Bin Abu Al A’ala,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Fasting one during the journey in a Month of Ramazan is like one not Fasting in it during the presence (at home)’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A man came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Can I Fast a Month of Ramazan during the journey?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘No’. So he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! It is easy upon me’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Gave charity upon the sick ones of my<sup>saww</sup> community and its travelers with the breaking (of the Fast) during a Month of Ramazan. Does it not astound one of you if he were to be given a charity that he would like to return it?’
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Utbah from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from Yahya ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who fasts on a journey in the month of Ramadan is like one who invalidates his fast while at home.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘Once a man came to the Holy prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and asked, “O Messenger of Allah, can I fast in the month of Ramadan on a journey?” He (the Messenger of Allah) replied, “No, you cannot fast on a journey.” He said, “O Messenger of Allah, it is very easy for me.” The Messenger of Allah said, “Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has given charity to those of my followers who are on a journey and those who are not in a good health to stop fasting in the month of Ramadan. Does it make any of you feel happy to reject a charity granted to you?””’
